text:
Sam O'Neill: Hey team — starting ~08:07 UTC we're seeing a sustained provisioning failure in ap-south1. New GPU node boot attempts are timing out during driver install. Pool utilization jumped to 92% and the autoscaler isn't achieving desired replicas.

Mia Chen: Noted. Is this the kernel/driver timeout we saw last month or a different failure mode?

Sam O'Neill: Logs look different — install hangs at 'nvidia-driver.service: start-post' repeatedly. Attaching tail: `Dec 12 08:05:13 node-034 systemd[1]: nvidia-driver.service: Start request repeated too quickly.`

Jordan Patel: ops-bot just pushed an alert: `AC40: ap-south1 provisioning-failure rate 18% (baseline 0.9%)`. I can start an emergency reroute to other AP regions if we want to avoid customer impact.

ops-bot: [ALERT] ap-south1: provisioning-failures > 10% for 4m. GPU_POOL_ap-south1 utilization=92%, queue_length=117.

Mia Chen: Let's throttle new allocations to ap-south1 and shift traffic. Plan: 1) set allocation weight ap-south1 -> 30% 2) shift remaining to ap-southeast1 and eu-south 3) start emergency on-demand instances in ap-southeast1 while we investigate driver hang.

Jordan Patel: Running traffic shift command now:
```
redwood route shift --region-from=ap-south1 --region-to=ap-southeast1,eu-south --percent=70 --policy=gradual --window=10m
```

KubeBot: Command accepted. Initiating gradual shift (70%) over 10m. Backpressure disabled for pinned workloads.

Alessandra Ruiz: Support here — drafting status page blurb. Suggest: short impact, who affected, ETA, mitigation steps. Can someone confirm customer-visible error types? Are API timeouts increasing or just queueing?

Sam O'Neill: Both increased: API token-level 504s for requests routed to new nodes (queue overflow) and provisioning 500s for new session creation. Error traces: `CreateSessionError: no resources available` and intermittent `504 upstream`.

Mia Chen: ETA: if we enable emergency on-demand from cloud quota and boot pre-baked image (skip post-install hooks) we can restore provisioning in ~28 minutes; full relief ~45 minutes once autoscaler stabilizes.

Jordan Patel: Cost note: emergency on-demand burst in ap-southeast1 estimated ~3.2k USD/hr while active. Approve?

Sam O'Neill: Approve. Prioritize customer availability. Please include cost heads-up to finance afterward.

Alessandra Ruiz: Draft status page update (please review):
"""
Incident: ap-south1 GPU provisioning errors — partial outage
Status: Investigating / Mitigating
Impact: New sessions provisioned in ap-south1 may fail or queue. Existing sessions largely unaffected. Some customers may experience elevated latency or 5xx errors when routed to ap-south1.
Mitigation: Traffic being shifted away from ap-south1 to neighboring regions. Emergency on-demand capacity being provisioned in ap-southeast1 to absorb traffic.
ETA: Initial mitigation in ~30 minutes, full mitigation in ~45 minutes.
Workaround: Customers can pin workloads to other regions (ap-southeast1, eu-south) via the 'region' parameter. See https://docs.redwood.ai/regions for instructions.
"""

Jordan Patel: Small wording tweak: change 'partial outage' -> 'degraded provisioning' and note cost-burst.

Alessandra Ruiz: Updated and posting to status.redwood.ai now.

Support Bot: [POSTED] https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1782105432 "ap-south1: degraded provisioning — traffic shift in progress" (public).

Sam O'Neill: Update from infra: driver install hang traced to a change in the OS image that introduced a race in nvidia post-install hook. Rolling back image in the provisioning pipeline now. This should stop new nodes from hitting the hang after boot.

Mia Chen: Rolling rollback completed for the image tag used by autoscaler group. New boots should skip the failing hook. Kicking a test boot now.

KubeBot: Test node boot SUCCESS. Provisioning latency 18s, driver service active.

Jordan Patel: Traffic shift progress: 70% shifted over 10m completed. Error rate for create-session routed to ap-south1 dropped from 1.2% -> 0.15%. Queue length down to 12.

Alessandra Ruiz: Updating status page: adding note that we have identified root cause and rollback applied. Keeping page 'investigating' -> 'monitoring'.

Sam O'Neill: Final note: We'll keep emergency on-demand capacity for 1 hour to ensure pool stability, then scale down gradually. Postmortem to follow with timeline and action items (image test gating).

Mia Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem doc and assign owners for image gating and deploy validation.

KubeBot: [CLOSED ALERT] AC40 resolved for ap-south1 (provisioning-failure rate normalized).

Alessandra Ruiz: Final status update posted: incident resolved, rollback applied, root cause identified, and timeline for postmortem. Customers notified via support.

Sam O'Neill: Closing thread here. Marking incident resolved at 08:45 UTC.
